newsitem.title: USA: Wheat harvest reported under way in south Nebraska.
newsitem.headline: Wheat harvest reported under way in south Nebraska.

text.p: Wheat combines began moving through fields in southern Nebraska last week although below normal temperatures slowed crop development, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
The harvest was three percent complete as of Sunday, down from 10 percent at the same time last year and a five-year average of 16 percent.

Winter wheat ratings declined slightly to three percent excellent, 44 good, 37 fair, 13 poor and three very poor. The crop was 29 percent ripe, up from 28 percent last year but behind the average of 46 percent.
The report noted irrigation systems were in full swing in the southwest and central parts of the state due to short moisture supplies.
Topsoil moisture was two percent surplus, 70 percent adequate, 25 percent short and three percent very short.
Some producers treated fields for corn borer. Corn was rated 17 percent excellent, 66 percent good, 14 percent fair, two percent poor and one percent very poor, little changed from a week earlier.
Soybean condition improved to 13 percent excellent, 68 percent good, 17 percent fair and two percent poor.
